topic_ko: 구조된 펭귄 Dindim이 해마다 약 5,000마일을 오가며 자신을 살려 준 노인에게 돌아온다

passage: In 2011 an elderly Brazilian named Joao Pereira de Souza was walking the beach of his island village near Rio de Janeiro.
There he came upon a penguin too weak to stand, its feathers heavy with oil.
He took the starving bird home, cleaned it, fed it, and called it Dindim.
When it was strong again he carried it back to the water and said goodbye for good.
The farewell did not last, because Dindim came back.
Experts believe the bird covers roughly 5,000 miles between the old man's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
It repeats that journey every single year without fail.
After about eight months at the village it leaves to breed, and then it returns once more.
choices: a rescued penguin's yearly return to the man who saved its life
the damage that oil spills cause to seabirds along the Brazilian coast
the migration routes that penguins follow between Argentina and Chile
the difficulty of raising wild animals inside a human household
the growing popularity of island villages near Rio de Janeiro
theme.explanation_ko: 구조된 펭귄이 해마다 먼 거리를 헤엄쳐 자신을 살려 준 노인에게 돌아온다는 이야기이므로 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② 기름 유출의 피해가 주제는 아니다. ③ 이동 경로 자체를 설명하는 글이 아니다. ④ 야생 동물 사육의 어려움은 언급이 없다. ⑤ 마을의 인기는 다루지 않는다.

passage: A retired fisherman on a small Brazilian island found a dying penguin on the sand in 2011.
Oil coated its body and it had not eaten for a long time.
He nursed the bird until its strength returned and then set it free.
He assumed he would never see the creature again.
Instead, Dindim swam back to him, and has done so ever since.
It is thought to travel about 5,000 miles between his house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
Each year it stays roughly eight months before leaving for its breeding grounds.
Every time, it makes the long trip home again.
choices: 구조된 야생 동물이 은인에게 놀라울 만큼 오래 이어지는 유대를 보이기도 한다.
펭귄은 인간의 도움 없이는 야생에서 살아남기 어렵다.
야생 동물은 한번 사람 손을 타면 이주 능력을 잃는다.
해양 오염을 막으려면 어민들의 협조가 반드시 필요하다.
번식기의 펭귄은 무리를 떠나 홀로 지내는 습성이 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 목숨을 구해 준 사람에게 해마다 수천 마일을 헤엄쳐 돌아오는 유대가 글의 요지이므로 ①이 적절하다.
gist.distractor_ko: ② 인간 없이 못 산다는 주장은 없다. ③ 이주 능력을 잃기는커녕 해마다 이주한다. ④ 어민의 협조는 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 무리를 떠나 홀로 지낸다는 서술은 없다.

passage: The beach of a small island near Rio de Janeiro held a strange sight in 2011.
A penguin lay struggling in the sand, helpless and covered in oil.
An old villager, Joao Pereira de Souza, carried it home and named it Dindim.
Weeks of care brought the bird back to health, and he released it into the sea.
He was certain the two would never meet again, but the penguin returned.
It is believed to swim some 5,000 miles between his door and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
Every year it spends about eight months with him before leaving to breed.
And every year, without fail, it comes back.
choices: The Penguin That Always Swims Home
Cleaning Oil from Seabirds: A Guide
Life in a Brazilian Island Village
title.explanation_ko: 해마다 반드시 돌아오는 펭귄이 이야기의 중심이므로 ①이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ② 세정 방법을 다루지 않는다. ③ 마을 생활은 배경일 뿐이다. ④ 이주의 일반적 이유가 아니다. ⑤ 최장 기록이라는 언급은 없다.

passage: In 2011 an old man on a Brazilian island found a penguin struggling on the beach.
The bird was starving and covered in oil, and he took it in and named it Dindim.
Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again.
The penguin, however, swam straight back to the village.
It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between the house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
What is more, he repeats this journey year after year.
He stays about eight months before leaving on his breeding migration.
Each time, he finds his way back to the same beach.
implication.underlined: Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again.
choices: He cared for the penguin until it recovered and then let it go, expecting a final parting.
He kept the penguin at home until it was healthy enough to be sold.
He treated the penguin quickly so that it would not become attached to him.
He released the penguin because he could no longer afford to feed it.
He hoped the penguin would soon bring other seabirds to the village.
implication.explanation_ko: 간호해 건강을 회복시킨 뒤 다시는 못 만날 것이라 여기며 놓아주었다는 뜻이므로 ①이 적절하다.
implication.distractor_ko: ② 판매 목적은 언급이 없다. ③ 정을 떼려 했다는 내용이 아니다. ④ 경제적 이유는 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 다른 새를 데려오리라는 기대는 없다.

passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, found a penguin struggling on the beach.
Covered in oil and close to starving, the helpless bird was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim.
He nursed the bird back to health and released it, thinking they would never meet again.
Amazingly, though, Dindim returned to the very same beach.
It is believed that he traveled some 5,000 miles between the old man's house and the far coasts of Argentina and Chile.
What is more, he makes this journey every year without fail.
After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only returning once again.
Nobody knows exactly how the bird finds its way.

underlines.text: was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named
It is believed that he traveled

grammar.explanation_ko: '떠났다가 결국 다시 돌아온다'라는 뜻밖의 결과를 나타내려면 결과를 뜻하는 to부정사 only to return 을 써야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① an old man 을 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사구로 적절하다. ② find 의 목적격보어 자리에 능동 의미의 현재분사가 온 형태이다. ③ was adopted 와 (was) named 가 병렬을 이루는 수동태이다. ④ 「It is believed that + 절」의 정상 형태이다.

passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, found a penguin struggling on the beach.
The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was abandoned by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim.
He nursed the bird back to health and released it, thinking they would never meet again.
Amazingly, though, Dindim returned to the village.
It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between the house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
What is more, he repeats this journey year after year.
After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine.
Yet he always comes back once again.
vocab.explanation_ko: 노인은 펭귄을 거두어 이름까지 붙여 주었으므로 abandoned(버려졌다)는 adopted(거두어졌다)가 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 해변에서 '힘겨워하는' 펭귄이므로 적절하다. ③ 건강을 되찾자 '놓아주었다'는 흐름에 맞는다. ④ 5,000마일을 '이동했다'는 의미로 옳다. ⑤ 해마다 하는 이주이므로 '연례의'가 알맞다.

passage: Joao Pereira de Souza expected nothing in return when he saved a dying penguin in 2011.
He washed the oil from its feathers, fed it for weeks, and named it Dindim.
Then he set it free on the shore, sure that the story had ended there.
Instead the bird came back, and it has come back every year since.
Between his house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile it swims some 5,000 miles.
About eight months of each year are spent at the village before the breeding season calls it away.
What the story suggests is that ______________________.
No fence and no cage holds the bird; it simply chooses the same beach.
choices: an act of kindness can create a bond that distance never breaks
wild animals lose their natural instincts once humans feed them
penguins prefer warm beaches to the cold waters of the south
rescued animals should always be kept away from their rescuers
long migrations are becoming shorter because of warmer seas
blank.explanation_ko: 우리에 갇힌 것도 아닌데 5,000마일을 헤엄쳐 같은 해변으로 돌아온다는 서술이 이어지므로, 친절이 거리로도 끊기지 않는 유대를 만든다는 ①이 적절하다.
blank.distractor_ko: ② 본능을 잃기는커녕 해마다 이주한다. ③ 따뜻한 해변을 선호한다는 내용이 아니다. ④ 은인과 떼어 놓아야 한다는 주장은 없다. ⑤ 바다 온난화는 언급되지 않았다.

irrelevant.intro: In 2011 Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, found a penguin struggling on the beach.
sentences: The helpless, starving creature was covered in oil, so he took it home and named it Dindim.
Emperor penguins in Antarctica are the tallest of all penguin species and can dive over five hundred meters.
After nursing the bird back to health he released it, thinking the two would never meet again.
Amazingly, Dindim returned, and is believed to travel around 5,000 miles between the house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.

irrelevant.explanation_ko: ②는 황제펭귄의 크기와 잠수 능력이라는 일반적 사실로, Dindim과 노인의 이야기 흐름에서 벗어난다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①③은 구조와 방생의 경위이고, ④⑤는 귀환과 반복되는 여정이라는 전개이므로 모두 흐름에 맞는다.

order.given: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature was covered in oil.

blocks.A: Amazingly, though, the bird returned to the very same beach. It is believed that he traveled some 5,000 miles between the old man's house and the far coasts of Argentina and Chile.
blocks.B: The old man took the bird in, named him Dindim, and nursed him back to health. When the penguin was strong again, he released him, thinking the two would never meet again.
blocks.C: What is more, he repeats this journey year after year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.

order.explanation_ko: 기름을 뒤집어쓴 펭귄의 발견(주어진 글) → 구조와 방생(B) → 뜻밖의 귀환과 5,000마일(A) → 해마다 반복되는 여정(C) 순이 자연스럽다.
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 'The old man took the bird in' 은 발견 직후에만 올 수 있고, (A)의 'Amazingly, though' 는 다시 못 만날 것이라 여긴 (B) 뒤라야 역접이 성립한다. (C)의 'this journey' 는 (A)에서 언급된 5,000마일의 여정을 받으므로 마지막이다.

insert.insert_sentence: He was convinced that the bird would vanish into the sea and never come near the village again.

passage_marked.text: In 2011 an old man in a Brazilian island village found a penguin struggling on the beach.
The starving creature was covered in oil, so he took it home and named it Dindim.
After weeks of care the bird grew strong, and Mr. de Souza carried it back to the shore and released it.
Amazingly, though, Dindim came back, and is believed to swim around 5,000 miles between the house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile.
He spends about eight months there each year before leaving on his breeding migration, only to return once again.

insert.explanation_ko: 다시는 오지 않으리라 확신했다는 문장은 방생 직후에 놓여야 하고, 뒤 문장의 'Amazingly, though' 가 그 확신을 뒤집으므로 ③이 적절하다.
insert.distractor_ko: ② 이전에 넣으면 아직 놓아주지 않은 상태라 확신할 대상이 없다. ④ 뒤에 넣으면 이미 돌아온 뒤여서 '사라질 것'이라는 확신이 모순된다.

passage: An old Brazilian villager found a penguin dying on the beach in 2011.
Its feathers were soaked in oil and it was close to starvation.
He carried it home, cared for it, and gave it the name Dindim.
Once the bird recovered he released it and expected never to see it again.
Dindim, however, swam back to the village.
The bird is thought to cover about 5,000 miles between the man's house and the southern coasts.
It stays roughly eight months each year before its breeding migration.
Then it turns around and comes home again.
summary.summary_template: Although Mr. de Souza expected their __(A)__ to be permanent, the penguin he had rescued now crosses thousands of miles each year to __(B)__ with him.
summary.explanation_ko: 노인은 그 '이별'이 영원할 것이라 여겼지만 펭귄은 해마다 돌아와 그와 '재회'하므로 parting–reunite 가 적절하다.
summary.distractor_ko: meeting·rescue 는 영원하리라 여겨진 대상이 아니고, compete(경쟁하다)는 둘 사이의 유대와 전혀 맞지 않는다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그 노인은 해변에서 힘겨워하고 있는 펭귄 한 마리를 발견했다.
writing.answer: The old man found a penguin struggling on the beach.
writing.explanation_ko: 「find + 목적어 + 현재분사」 구조로, 목적어가 능동적으로 그 동작을 하고 있음을 나타낸다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그는 번식을 위한 이주를 떠나지만, 결국 또다시 돌아온다.
conditions: 결과를 나타내는 only to V 를 사용할 것
goes on his annual migration 을 사용할 것
once again 으로 문장을 끝낼 것
writing.answer: He goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.
writing.explanation_ko: only to V 는 '(결국) ~하고 만다'라는 뜻밖의 결과를 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사이다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: Mr. de Souza released the bird because he thought it belonged in the sea, and he was sure they would never ___________ again.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 노인은 다시는 만나지 못할 것이라고 생각하며 놓아주었으므로 meet 이 적절하다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Covered in oil and close to starving, the helpless bird was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim.
writing.answer: 기름을 뒤집어쓴 채 굶주리고 있던 그 무력한 생명체는 de Souza 씨에게 거두어져 Dindim이라는 이름을 얻었다.
writing.explanation_ko: covered in oil 은 creature 를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사구이고, was adopted 와 (was) named 가 병렬을 이루는 수동태이다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Dindim is believed to travel around 5,000 __(A)__ each year, spending about eight __(B)__ with Mr. de Souza before his migration.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 이동 거리는 around 5,000 miles 이고, 노인과 함께 지내는 기간은 about eight months 이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: penguin 과 return 을 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: A rescued penguin swims thousands of miles every year to return to the man who saved him.
writing.explanation_ko: 구조된 사실과 해마다 은인에게 돌아온다는 핵심을 한 문장에 담으면 된다.
